title: 7 · File I/O (Deep Dive)
learn:
The story: notebooks that survive power cuts

Variables are a whiteboard wiped when the program ends. Files are notebooks that stay. File I/O means reading from and writing to them. All the classes live in java.io (plus Scanner in java.util).

Reading text: Scanner + FileReader

Scanner sc = new Scanner(new FileReader("data.txt")); FileReader opens the file, Scanner gives you the friendly methods you already know. Read until the file runs out: while (sc.hasNextLine()) sc.nextLine();. Match the method to the data: hasNextInt()/nextInt() for numbers, nextDouble(), next() for words, nextLine() for whole lines. Always close() when finished.

Writing text: PrintWriter

PrintWriter out = new PrintWriter("output.txt"); then println and print, exactly like System.out. You must close() (or flush) it, otherwise the text may stay in a buffer and never reach the file. By default it overwrites an existing file; to append, wrap a FileWriter opened with true: new PrintWriter(new FileWriter("log.txt", true)).

Why exceptions appear

The file might not exist, be locked, or the path might be wrong. Java makes you deal with it. Two choices: try/catch (handle it here) or throws (hand the responsibility up to the caller, and eventually the JVM). FileReader throws FileNotFoundException; broader problems throw IOException.

try-with-resources

Put the resource in the parentheses after try and Java closes it for you, even if an error occurs: try (Scanner sc = ...) { ... } catch (...) { ... }. This is the cleanest exam answer.

Paths

A relative path (data.txt) starts from the program's working folder. An absolute path (C:/data/data.txt) starts from the drive root. Use forward slashes or doubled backslashes in strings.

Common file-reading patterns

Sum of numbers on a line: loop with hasNextInt(). Count lines: counter in a hasNextLine loop. Search a word: compare each line with contains() or equals(). Parse a CSV line with StringTokenizer or split(","). The exam question about summing 22 33 44 55 66 from a file is exactly the first pattern.
